findings.claim: "The library's argument: a software business with brittle safety culture cannot run a blameless postmortem, and a software business without blameless postmortems cannot learn from incidents at a rate that preserves customer trust."; line 20 "The library's position: ... cannot surface the failure modes that erode customer trust."

notes: Source line numbers refer to corpus.commons/demo/sources/converted/open-practice-library.md. Deep-ref fixes surfaced: (1) line 330 lists 'Schwaber & Sutherland' among authors OPL practices cite; the source never cites them. (2) line 32 lists Test Automation and TDD under Delivery; both carry mobiusTag foundation (source L8390, L8451), as line 122 and this distillation correctly say. (3) line 127 says the substrate practices are 'tagged methods and culture rather than delivery', conflating tags with mobiusTag ('delivery' is not a tag value; Container and Defence in Depth carry no tags). Integration claims checked: jones (folklore line 15), letaw (RACI, triple constraint, microservices, Tuckman present), scrum-guide-2020 (lines 35, 39), approach-perfect-field-guide, open-kanban (lines 58-87), nhs-just-culture-guide, tc-25-20, lfuo (three principles line 7), openstax-principles-management (Tuckman, Hofstede, structures, motivation present), openstax-organizational-behavior (groupthink, escalation, process/relationship conflict present), openstax-business-ethics (line 111), openstax-accounting-vol2 (relevant cost, CVP, break-even, ToC, cost classification present). The lens section was audited only for its claims about the source.
